ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed directors, managers, statutory auditors, shareholders above 25% and UBOs against (i) the French national asset-freeze and politically-exposed-person lists maintained by the Direction générale du Trésor, (ii) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list under Common Foreign and Security Policy, (iii) United Nations Security Council consolidated lists, (iv) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals sanctions for USD-related transactions, and (v) AMF watchlists; given the ISIC 5210 bonded warehouse operation classified as Medium_Risk_Enhanced, Enhanced Due Diligence is compulsory and includes adverse media review, source of wealth documentation, and annual re-screening for the duration of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, with name availability verified through the Infogreffe database of the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A French SARL may adopt a denommation sociale in any language, but the name must be lawful, distinctive, and not contrary to public order or good morals; if the name includes non-French characters, a Latin-alphabet transliteration and a French-language operating name are required for French public notices, contracts, and customs appointments; the name must not be misleading as to corporate form, activity, or nationality of the company.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, Bancaire, Crédit, Financement (credit institution approval under CMF required)
Assurance, Mutuelle, Réassurance (insurance regulatory approval required)
Syndicat, Ordre, Chambre professionnelle (regulated professional body consent required)
Ministère, République, État, National, Français (misleading state affiliation, ministerial authorization required)
Securité, Défense, Douanes (sensitive strategic sector prior clearance required)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Under the July 2021 company law reform and the INPI guichet unique system, there is no separate pre-registration name certificate; the proposed denommation sociale is checked for availability and legal admissibility at filing. If the INPI system or the competent Greffe rejects the name, the applicant may resubmit the formalities with a corrected name without penalty. In the event of formal refusal, an administrative appeal must be lodged with the Director General of INPI within two months of refusal notification. Judicial recourse thereafter lies before the specialized commercial chamber of the Tribunal judiciaire of the registered office seat, with the assistance of a French avocat.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for the registered office of an SARL under Article L123-11-2 of the French Commercial Code and Article R123-187 of the Commercial Code through an approved domiciliation company or approved business incubator, for a maximum initial term of three years subject to renewal; however, the customs-bonded depot and any operational or storage premises must be physical sites physically located inside an authorized customs free-zone area and cannot be virtualized.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High for the bonded depot itself at approximately 70%-80% annual likelihood, because customs-free-zone and entrepôt sous douane operations are subject to continuous customs supervision under the EU Union Customs Code (Regulation EU 952/2013, Articles 211 and 242) and to unannounced physical inspections by the Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects; by contrast, the registered-office correspondence address is treated as a lower-risk administrative location with a physical inspection likelihood below 10% unless financial or sanctions anomalies are identified.

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital of 1 EUR fully subscribed and paid at incorporation; no escrow account required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The founding shareholder resolves unanimously: (1) to subscribe to and pay in full the entire share capital of 1,000 EUR; (2) to adopt the registered office at [Insert full address], France; (3) to appoint [Full Name] as Président, [Full Name] as gérant, and [Full Name] as commissaire aux comptes; (4) to approve the Articles of Association including the bonded warehouse depot purpose; (5) to authorize all filing and incorporation actions. This resolution governs initial governance until the first general meeting.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: French Directorate General of Public Finances (Direction générale des finances publiques, DGFiP), acting through the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the impots.gouv.fr portal. Business incorporation and enterprise identifiers are administered through the Guichet unique operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI); customs matters are administered by the Directorate General of Customs and Indirect Taxes (Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects, DGDDI) through the French customs online services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SARL is incorporated through the Guichet unique, which transmits registration data to the competent registries and tax authorities. The entity receives a SIREN identifier and establishment-level SIRET identifier. The French VAT number is issued by the DGFiP and normally has the format FR followed by a two-character control key and the nine-digit SIREN. The entity must submit the required tax registration and VAT information to the competent SIE, including legal documents, registered office details, beneficial-owner information, business activities, expected turnover, bank details, accounting period, and evidence of taxable transactions where requested. A foreign entity without a French establishment that performs taxable French transactions must apply for French VAT registration with the non-established-taxable-persons service of the DGFiP. EU-established businesses generally do not require a French tax representative; non-EU businesses normally require an accredited French tax representative unless a specific statutory exemption applies. Customs operations additionally require an Economic Operators Registration and Identification (EORI) number obtained through French customs. A customs warehouse or bonded-depot operator must obtain the relevant customs authorisation and comply with the Union Customs Code, including inventory, guarantee, recordkeeping, and control requirements.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL is subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) by default. Subject to statutory conditions, a SARL may elect for income-tax treatment (impôt sur le revenu, IR), including the family SARL regime where all shareholders are qualifying family members and the company conducts an eligible commercial, industrial, artisanal, or professional activity. Certain closely held SARLs may also elect temporarily for IR treatment for up to five financial years if the statutory ownership, size, age, and activity conditions are satisfied. France has no US-style check-the-box election. French anti-hybrid-mismatch rules implement the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive framework and generally operate as mandatory anti-abuse rules rather than elective classification mechanisms. Separate elections may apply to VAT filing regimes, including the franchise in base, simplified regime, or normal regime, subject to statutory eligibility.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, VAT), supplemented by customs duties, excise duties, and other indirect taxes. France is part of the EU VAT territory, subject to EU VAT Directive rules and the Union Customs Code.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a business making taxable French supplies, including a non-established business, there is generally no minimum turnover threshold before French VAT registration becomes necessary; the practical threshold is EUR 0 where a taxable transaction requires French VAT reporting and no reverse-charge or other exemption applies. The domestic franchise in base may exempt qualifying small businesses from charging VAT, subject to turnover limits. The principal 2025 thresholds are generally EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods, accommodation, and certain restaurant activities, with a tolerance threshold of EUR 93,500, and EUR 37,500 for services and non-commercial activities, with a tolerance threshold of EUR 41,250. These thresholds and their application are subject to statutory amendments and should be verified for the relevant tax year. Intra-EU distance-sales and electronically supplied services are subject to separate EU-wide EUR 10,000 thresholds and OSS rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory domestic business-to-business electronic invoicing and electronic transaction reporting through approved private platforms connected to the public directory. All businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices from 1 September 2026. Issuance obligations begin on 1 September 2026 for large enterprises and groups subject to the large-enterprise rules, and on 1 September 2027 for medium-sized and smaller businesses, subject to legislative and regulatory updates. Domestic B2B electronic invoices must use a permitted structured or hybrid format and contain required invoice data. E-reporting applies to specified cross-border transactions and business-to-consumer transactions. France does not currently operate a universal real-time VAT invoice-clearance or pre-issuance tax-stamping system for ordinary domestic invoices. Public-sector invoices are generally submitted through Chorus Pro. Customs declarations and warehouse records may require electronic filing through DGDDI systems and must support audit trails, stock reconciliation, and customs-control access.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to a destination outside the EU VAT territory may be invoiced without French VAT where the statutory export conditions are met, including export by the French seller or by a qualifying intermediary, or export by the customer under the applicable rules, and proof that the goods physically left the EU. The principal evidence is an accepted customs export declaration linked to an electronic exit result or equivalent customs evidence. Supplies placed under qualifying customs warehousing, free-zone, transit, or other suspensive procedures may receive special VAT treatment, but the treatment is not automatically equivalent to an export and depends on the precise customs procedure and place of supply. Services supplied to a business established outside France may be outside the scope of French VAT under the B2B place-of-supply rule rather than zero-rated exports; the supplier must substantiate customer business status, contractual scope, place of establishment, and absence of a French fixed establishment receiving the service. Intra-EU supplies of goods are generally exempt with credit rather than exports and require valid customer VAT identification and transport evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration containing the export MRN and accepted export data
Electronic confirmation of exit from the EU customs territory or equivalent certified customs evidence
Commercial invoice identifying the exporter, customer, goods, value, VAT treatment, and delivery terms
Packing list and transport documentation, such as bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, or courier manifest
Proof of delivery or other transport-chain evidence where required to corroborate physical exit
Customs warehouse, free-zone, or transit records, stock records, and release or discharge evidence where a suspensive customs procedure is used
Contract, purchase order, and customer correspondence supporting the export transaction
Bank payment evidence where relevant to commercial substantiation; an inward-remittance certificate is not generally a mandatory French VAT export document
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds because France uses the euro and does not impose a general export-proceeds repatriation regime. Export VAT exemption or refund claims may be denied or clawed back where customs exit evidence is missing, contradictory, falsified, obtained after the fact without adequate linkage, or inconsistent with transport, stock, invoicing, or accounting records. Under the French tax procedure, ordinary VAT reassessment periods generally extend through the end of the third year following the year in which the tax became payable, subject to special rules and extensions for fraud or criminal proceedings. Late-payment interest is generally charged at the statutory rate, commonly 0.20% per month, subject to applicable amendments. Tax penalties may include a 10% surcharge for late payment or filing, 40% for deliberate non-compliance, and up to 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of rights, subject to statutory conditions and procedural safeguards. Fraudulent customs declarations may trigger recovery of customs duties and VAT, administrative fines, seizure or forfeiture measures, withdrawal of customs authorisations, and potential criminal liability under French and EU customs law. A bonded warehouse operator may also face suspension or revocation of its customs authorisation, guarantee enforcement, duty and VAT recovery, and liability for inventory discrepancies or unauthorised removal of goods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, acting as agent for the European Central Bank for euro monetary policy and as national supervising authority for credit institutions; the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) exercises foreign exchange and external financial sanctions coordination, while the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) supervises banks and payment institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully and freely convertible in France. Both current and capital account transactions are liberalized within the European Union under Articles 63 to 66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. No prior exchange control authorization is required for equity capital subscriptions, shareholder loans, trade payments, or profit repatriation. Constraints are limited to sanctions screening, customs related identity checks for free trade zone operators, and the corporate law conditions for SARL dividend distributions: annual accounts must be approved by shareholders, distributable profit must exist, and net assets must not fall below unpaid capital plus non-distributable reserves. Neither branch profit remittance nor dividend payment is subject to exchange control approval, though dividends derived from an active logistics entity may carry a domestic withholding tax and require a tax residence certificate when the recipient is treaty-entitled.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France maintains no export proceeds surrender obligation and imposes no mandatory conversion ratio or statutory repatriation timeline. Export receipts may be retained in any currency and converted at market rates. However, under customs law, records of physical and financial flows for goods entered into a bonded warehouse in a free trade zone must be kept in the approved customs accounting regime and presented to the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) on demand. Payment evidence, banking advices, and SWIFT messages must be archived for at least the statutory customs record retention period to demonstrate physical movement, value, and settlement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational account (compte à vue) plus separate capital escrow/blocked deposit account for injected share capital; trade finance and LC capability.
Operational account, customs guarantee line, and FX hedging facilities for cross-border trade settlement.
Operational account and local clearing concentration account, suitable for domestic payments and Treasury pooling.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Conditional feasibility rating: Medium. A fintech electronic money institution (EMI) holding or passported under the EU Payment Services Directive (PSD2) and registered with the ACPR may legally provide payment services, issue e-money accounts, and support cross-border euro disbursements. However, EMIs are not credit institutions and cannot hold capital deposits, provide credit, issue documentary credits, or act as escrow agents for share capital in the same manner as banks. For a bonded depot company classified as Medium_Risk_Enhanced, reliance on an EMI is suitable only for narrowly tailored operational payables, not for statutory capital escrow, customs guarantees, supplier LCs, or permanent treasury concentration. Concentration risk and the absence of a credit relationship must be mitigated through a back-to-back arrangement with an ACPR-licensed bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a non-resident-owned SARL engaged in free trade zone bonded depot operations, a physical KYC interview is generally required by French tier-1 institutions during initial onboarding. Remote opening is possible in select cases using French electronic identification with video verification, but enhanced due diligence for this sector usually requires at least one director or authorized signatory to appear in person, or an equivalent attendance by a notarized French-based agent with a power of attorney. If the managing director cannot attend, a French lawyer or certified accountant empowered under an original notarized power of attorney can help complete the interview, but the bank retains the right to demand physical presence where the ultimate beneficial owner is located outside the EEA.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed or partially visible ultimate beneficial owner structure, particularly holdings through low-tax or non-cooperative jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized French or internationally apostilled constitutional documents, current RCS Kbis extract, a complete UBO register declaration filed in France, passport copies of all natural persons with direct or indirect ownership above 25%, a corporate tree with percentage holdings, source-of-wealth brief, and legal opinions confirming the lawful provenance of capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Free trade zone and bonded depot activity flag as higher risk because of deferred customs duty, potential excise diversion, counterfeit goods exposure, and reduced customs supervision.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid DGDDI operating license or warehouse declaration for the bonded facility, detailed logistics standard operating procedures, inventory management system audit report, physical security report, customs bond or comprehensive guarantee certificates, tariff classification policy, and a signed undertaking to deliver customs stock accounts on demand.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border payments to sanctions-sensitive geographies or unfamiliar trading counterparties, triggering transaction monitoring alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete underlying commercial contracts, pro forma invoices, packing lists, transport documents (CMR, bill of lading, airway bill), Incoterms evidence, insurance certificates, sanctions and PEP screening reports, counterparty trade-references, and an annual external audit covering both financial statements and trade flows.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Contribute capital from the non-resident shareholder to the French SARL using SWIFT MT103 or MT202 with the beneficiary IBAN and SARL legal name. Reference the payment as 'Capital subscription / Apport en capital / Constitution de SARL' and retain the bank attestation (attestation de dépôt des fonds) issued by the receiving bank for use before the notary at the RCS registration. No prior Bank of France exchange approval is required because the flow is a eurozone or convertible-currency equity investment. Where the injection exceeds EUR 10,000 in physical cash or bearer instruments, customs cash-control declarations apply, but bank-wired funds are not subject to monetary declaration thresholds. Confirm that the payer bank conducts sanctions and PEP screening, and include a board resolution or shareholder resolution authorizing the contribution to satisfy internal controls.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for non-European Economic Area supplier payments in EUR or USD, with full invoice references and country-specific purpose codes required by the intermediary banks. For large warehouse replenishment acquisitions, an irrevocable documentary commercial letter of credit issued through a French tier-1 bank and advised via SWIFT MT700 is preferred; settlement occurs on presentation of compliant shipping documents under UCP600. For payments within the SEPA zone, use local SEPA credit transfers with the beneficiary IBAN, but maintain segregated trade-payment accounts to reduce AML noise. Customs duties, VAT, and other bonded-goods obligations are settled through local French clearing rails, with bank guarantees (garantie de la douane) or cash collateral lodged in favor of the DGDDI.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright forward contracts with ACPR-licensed credit institutions, executed under an ISDA or French forward framework and subject to EMIR obligations where applicable.
EUR/USD and EUR/GBP FX swaps (swap de change) for short-term liquidity and working capital optimization.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for medium-term matching of currency-denominated asset and liability positions.
Vanilla EUR foreign exchange options for hedging adverse currency movements in large long-dated commercial contracts.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted currencies only where the underlying currency is illiquid or impossible to deliver physically; in France, the euro is fully deliverable, so NDFs are generally unnecessary and are permissible only with an ACPR-licensed counterparty and documented hedge intent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale) – déclaration de résultats, form 2065-series and annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques – Service des Impôts des Entreprises of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months of the financial year-end; for a calendar-year SARL the e-filing deadline is the second business day after 1 May of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax due if filed within 30 days after the deadline, increased to 10% after 30 days, plus monthly late-payment interest; intentional non-filing may trigger a 40% penalty and criminal tax sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' approval and deposit of the annual accounts (dépôt des comptes annuels) with the commercial register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the INPI Guichet des Formalités des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual general meeting must approve the accounts within six months of the financial year-end; the depository filing must be lodged within one month of approval. For a 31 December year-end, approval by 30 June and filing by 31 July is the practical outer limit.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of up to €1,500 for the company manager, increased to €3,000 on repeated default; the commercial court may impose astreinte (coercive fine) and persistent non-filing may lead to administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual customs inventory reconciliation statement for the bonded warehouse / free-trade-zone stock register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Régionale des Douanes et Droits Indirects
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the customs authorization accounting closing date, commonly 31 January for a calendar-year storage cycle, unless otherwise stated in the warehouse authorization.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Customs fines under the French Customs Code, possible suspension or revocation of the bonded warehouse authorization, and disqualification of the warehouse operator for false or late stock declarations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit for a French SARL where at least two of the following thresholds are exceeded at the balance-sheet date: total assets €4,000,000; net turnover excluding VAT €8,000,000; and an average employee count of 50 over the financial year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan comptable général, as regulated by the Autorité des Normes Comptables) is the mandatory framework for the statutory annual accounts of an SARL; IFRS applies only to consolidated accounts of certain groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The French beneficial-owner declaration is filed at registration and updated with the commercial registry within 30 days after any change in beneficial ownership; there is no separate annual UBO renewal filing. The annual general meeting must reconcile share transfers and update the register of members before approving the annual accounts.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 130 – USD 330 per year for domiciliation agent and registered-office services for a small-to-mid-size SARL.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,400 – USD 13,000 per year for a certified audit of a mid-size SARL, subject to complexity, inventory valuation, and French customs-stock review requirements.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard corporate income tax rate is 25% for profits from 1 January 2023. A reduced effective rate of 15% applies to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit per 12-month period, subject to a EUR 500,000 taxable profit threshold. The French Research Tax Credit (CIR) provides a 30% credit on eligible R&D expenses up to EUR 100 million. No zone-specific income tax holiday applies to free trade zone or bonded warehouse operators; customs and VAT suspension benefits do not relieve corporate income tax. Loss carryforward is subject to an annual deduction cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of the excess taxable income, while the carryback window under French law is capped at EUR 1 million over 5 fiscal years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (Déclaration de Résultats) and liasse fiscale annexes 2050 to 2059-G; filed electronically through the DGFiP 'Gérer mon entreprise' portal (TéléIRIS/EFI platform) in standard XBRL/GJ format.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return plus quarterly corporate income tax instalments for companies whose prior-year corporate income tax exceeded EUR 10,000; the final balancing payment is made with the annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within 60 days after the close of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year entity closing on 31 December, the administrative filing calendar grants a deferral generally until the second business day after 1 May (e.g., 3 May 2024). Non-calendar fiscal years are due 60 days from the fiscal year close.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Chiffre d'affaires et recettes (gross French revenue exclusive of VAT and customs duty).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only revenue attributable to the French permanent establishment or the French fixed-place bonded operation; exclude sales booked through a foreign principal unless a dependent agent French PE exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cadre B, Resultat fiscal avant report
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net profit before tax adjustments, before deduction of loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the French PE accounting profit in compliance with French GAAP; if the entity is a single-purpose bonded warehouse SARL, include all warehouse fees, handling charges, and inventory write-downs deriving from the French activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of prior-year French tax losses subject to the annual EUR 1 million plus 50% excess cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses generated by the same French PE or French legal entity are reportable; foreign head-office losses cannot be offset against French taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cadre D, Régime des sociétés et groupements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of option or normal rules for corporate tax liability and status of the SARL.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm the SARL is not part of a tax consolidation group unless a French 'intégration fiscale' election exists; foreign parent revenues are not reported here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation, provisions, and exceptional charges used to arrive at the fiscally adjusted taxable result.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Keep asset registers for warehouse equipment and leasehold improvements physically located in France; no depreciation on foreign head-office assets may be claimed in the French PE return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of transactions with related parties, method applied, and financial counterparties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose cross-border warehouse handling fees, inventory management fees, or intercompany charges with foreign affiliates under Art. L13 AA/L13 AB CGI and update with current transfer pricing documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a statutory 5% late filing penalty on the amount of tax due, increased to 10% after a formal notice. Overdue tax carries late-payment interest (intérêt de retard) at 0.20% per month; an additional 40% 'bad faith' penalty applies to non-disclosed income, and an 80% penalty applies to abusive concealment or abuse of law. Missing ancillary schedules in the liasse fiscale attract EUR 15 per omission under the electronic filing rules, plus possible administrative injunctions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% for dividends distributed by a French company to non-resident corporate beneficial owners (Article 119 bis 2 of the French General Tax Code); 30% for non-resident individual beneficial owners under the single flat levy. An EU qualified parent may benefit from a 0% dividend withholding tax under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive subject to the 5% or 10% holding conditions and required holding period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced withholding rate under a French tax treaty, the beneficial owner must obtain a certificate of tax residence (Form 5000 or a treaty-prescribed certificate) issued by the foreign tax administration, endorse it with a signed claim of beneficial ownership, and transmit it to the French paying agent before the distribution or to the competent DGFiP service for a refund. For relief at source, the certificate must be deposited with the French withholding agent; for refunds, a claim must be filed within the applicable statutory limitation period (generally before 31 December of the second year following the income realisation). The French tax administration may deny the benefit where the recipient lacks economic substance, substance-related beneficial ownership, or the principal purpose of the structure is treaty abuse.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory royalty withholding for patents, trademarks, copyright and industrial know-how paid to non-residents is 33.33% of gross royalties. Most French tax treaties reduce this to 5% or 10% (often 5% for equipment and 10% for patent royalties), subject to beneficial ownership. Interest paid to non-residents on ordinary commercial loans is generally exempt from French withholding tax; interest on bearer notes and certain financial instruments is subject to statutory withholding at 12.8% (Article 125 A), with treaty rates generally reduced to 0% or 10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million in annual net French turnover (excluding VAT) for the French entity, or EUR 400 million in gross assets, or membership in a group with consolidated worldwide revenue exceeding EUR 750 million; at any such threshold, the entity must prepare and maintain a Master File and Local File under Articles L13 AA and L13 AB of the French Book of Tax Procedures. Below the threshold, entities must still retain adequate comparability and arm's-length justification for related-party transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply a stand-alone 'Economic Substance Regulation' regime like certain free-trade-zone jurisdictions. Instead, the French tax administration uses the 'abus de droit' doctrine (Article L64 of the Book of Tax Procedures), the anti-hybrid and principal-purpose tests under EU and OECD Base Erosion and Profit Shifting, and the concept of abuse of law to attack tax-motivated arrangements lacking real substance. A bonded warehouse SARL must demonstrate actual operational presence in France: a valid French customs bonded-warehouse authorisation, owned or leased physical premises, licensed staff exercising management and custody over the inventory, its own stock records, and authority over commercial decisions. A nominally registered SARL acting solely as a conduit or invoicing vehicle for a foreign principal will not be recognised.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Undeclared Bonded Sales
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission or suppression of taxable profits arising from release of bonded goods into free circulation, unrecorded cash sales, false customs stock records, or diversion of sales revenue to foreign bank accounts without inclusion in the French corporate income tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalty for fiscal fraud under Article 1741 of the French General Tax Code: a fine of up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years, increased to EUR 3,000,000 and 7 years for aggravated fraud involving computer misuse or organised crime. Civil sanctions include the 80% concealment penalty, late-payment interest at 0.20% monthly, and reassessment of the full evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing directors and de facto officers who personally conceive, orchestrate or sign false declarations are jointly and severally liable for corporate tax, penalties and interest; personal travel bans, loss of civil rights, restriction of professional activity, and, upon criminal conviction, imprisonment up to 7 years are applicable. The corporate veil may be pierced where the SARL has been used as a sham or fraudulent conduit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abuse of Law / Artificial Shell Arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing or maintaining the SARL with no genuine commercial substance, no independent operational power over bonded goods, no legitimate warehouse workforce, or using a French registered vehicle solely to access free-zone customs benefits or treaty conditions while the real decision-making and profits remain outside France.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article L64 of the Book of Tax Procedures authorises the tax administration to disregard the artificial act and reattribute the concealed profits to the French entity or principal; the abusive arrangement carries an 80% penalty (majoration d'abus de droit), or 10% if a legitimate non-tax reason exists, plus interest. The relevant customs free-zone status may also be revoked and duties recovered.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who have personally approved or implemented the sham arrangement may be held personally liable for the reassessed corporate income tax and penalties under the manager's civil liability regime; in aggravated cases, personal indictment for tax evasion or company assets misuse is possible with potential travel bans and managerial disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and Deficient Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare, update or produce the Local File/Master File when the French SARL exceeds the statutory documentation threshold, or charging non-arm's-length handling fees, management fees, royalties or interest to foreign affiliates or an importer of record operating in the bonded supply chain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax administration may reconstruct the taxable profit at arm's length; the lack of compliant documentation triggers the penalty regime under Article L13 B of the Book of Tax Procedures, a mandatory 5% penalty on reassessed profits where documentation is not produced, and an automatic 40% bad-faith penalty or 80% gross-negligence penalty, plus late-payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who have signed false or incomplete transfer pricing declarations or approved artificial service fees can be held personally liable for tax recalculations and penalties; if the TP manipulation constitutes the stripping of profits through sham contracts, directors may additionally face 'abus de biens sociaux' civil liability and professional restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and Customs Fraud in the Free Trade Zone
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowledge or suspected use of bonded warehouse, free-zone stock or customs documents to launder criminally derived funds, accepting unexplained third-party settlements for bonded goods, deliberately making false customs declarations in the free-zone stock accounting, or failing to maintain the statutory beneficial-owner register and AML compliance controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the French Monetary and Financial Code, money laundering by a legal person is punishable by a fine equal to five times the fines applicable to individuals (up to EUR 1,875,000 for individuals? Actually individuals up to EUR 375,000, legal persons up to EUR 1,875,000) and/or up to 5 years' imprisonment for individual operators. Customs fraud sanctions include confiscation of the goods, a fine of one to five times the value of the fraudulent merchandise, and revocation of the customs bonded-warehouse licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate, fail to implement AML measures, or allow the SARL to be used for laundering proceeds are jointly civilly liable for fines and forfeiture, personally exposed to criminal money-laundering charges (up to 5 years' imprisonment for individuals and EUR 375,000 fine), and subject to travel bans, professional disqualification, and removal from management positions.
